spots.note: 15:32 afternoon run. Cam clear, bright full daylight, water readable edge to edge. Surface is wind-torn by the 18g23kt N cross-shore - heavy texture everywhere, waves breaking well outside as short crumbling sections that never stand up as a green wall; the whitewater is patchy and sectiony rather than one long peeling line. Scanned takeoff zone, both shoulders and the inside in all 3 detail frames and both crowd frames: no bodies, no boards, no paddling lines. Confident 0 out. One person leaning on the promenade wall at the right edge of the frame, but the cam is framed on the water so land count not applicable

15:32 afternoon run. Water fully legible, no glare, no blowout. The bay is very weak: thin reform lines sliding in towards the rock point with almost no height and no face ahead of the foam, plus uniform wind ripple across the whole bay. Nothing stands up in any of the 3 detail frames or the 6 sheet frames. Scanned the open bay, the corner by the rocks and the shorebreak in every frame: nobody in the water. 0 out, and with this little wave that is expected rather than a wasted lineup. Cam framed on the water, land count not applicable

15:32 afternoon run - cam UP again (second good run in a row after the sunrise 404). Sunny, deep blue, good visibility. Still the only working spot: waist-high lines breaking along the reef with a green face ahead of the foam in several frames, held up by the 18g23kt N blowing offshore here, but distinctly bumpier than the 11:31 run - 23kt gusts are putting chatter on the faces. Count is approximate: a scattered line of roughly 8 dark specks sitting out the back on the outside line, consistent across the +0s and +12s sheet frames, plus 3-4 resolvable in the crowd crops inside that same zone (higher of the two frames). Heavy wind chop makes an exact count impossible so 8 is a floor-ish read, not a precise figure. On land roughly 25: about 6 along the promenade railing and 15-20 sitting or walking on the sand. 8 out is right on the 8.0 average for this slot

15:32 afternoon run, wide distant cam so all counts approximate. Cam clean and bright. Wave is closing out badly: a continuous wall of whitewater across the whole beach dumping straight onto the sand, wind-chopped by the 18g23kt N cross-shore, no bank holding any shape - matches the VERY_POOR rating. Opened the detail crop and scanned the whole waterline in all 3 frames plus both crowd frames: no boards, nobody sitting outside the whitewater. Two dark specks standing in the shorebreak shallows near the lifeguard flag are bathers, not surfers, so 0 surfing rather than null. On land roughly 30: scattered groups and tents along the sand, a beach-volleyball style cluster at the right by the promenade, a few walking

11:31 lunch run. Cam clear, full daylight, no glare. Tide near the 11:08 low so the reef shelf is half dry - large areas of exposed rock and drained pools across the whole inside. What swell there is breaks well outside as short weak crumbly lines over the shallow shelf, chopped by the 18g21kt N cross-shore; nothing stands up as a green wall. Scanned takeoff zone, both shoulders and the inside channel in all 3 detail frames and both crowd frames: no bodies, no boards, no paddling lines anywhere in the water. Confident 0 out - the reef is simply not surfable at this tide and size. One person walking on the dry rock shelf. Cam framed on the water, land count not applicable

11:31 lunch run. Water fully readable, bright and legible edge to edge, no blowout. The bay is effectively flat: uniform wind ripple with only a thin wash breaking on the exposed rocks along the right-hand side, and reef showing through the shallows. No swell line stands up anywhere in the 3 detail frames or the 6 sheet frames. Scanned the open bay, the corner by the rocks and the shorebreak in every frame: nobody in the water. 0 out, and given how flat it is that is expected rather than a wasted lineup. Cam framed on the water, land count not applicable

11:31 lunch run - CAM IS BACK UP after being 404/dead at the 09:10 sunrise run. Sunny, deep blue water, excellent visibility. Best spot by a distance: clean waist-high lines peeling right along the reef with an unbroken green face ahead of the foam in several frames, held up and groomed by the 18kt N wind blowing offshore here. Counted in the crowd crops (higher of the two frames): a cluster of roughly 6-7 sitting/paddling in the left third plus 3 further out towards the middle peak, so 10 in the water; a couple more ambiguous specks not counted. On land 2 people standing out on the rock shelf in the crowd crops, plus roughly 10 more on the sand and along the promenade railing in the contact sheet - about 12 total, approximate. 10 out is below the 16.7 average for this slot

11:31 lunch run, wide distant cam so land counts approximate. Cam clean and bright, no glare. Wave is closing out: a continuous wall of whitewater running the length of the beach and dumping straight onto the sand, wind-chopped by the 18g21kt N cross-shore, no bank holding any shape - this reads worse than the POOR rating and matches the VERY_POOR it drops to from 15:00. Opened the detail crop and scanned the whole waterline in all 3 frames plus both crowd frames: no boards and nobody sitting outside the whitewater. A few dark specks are standing in the shorebreak inside the lifeguard-flagged zone - bathers, not surfers - so 0 surfing rather than null. On land roughly 20: a scatter of sitting groups and two tents along the top of the sand, a few walking, plus a handful by the rocks at the far end

08:56 sunrise run (task ran late). Cam clear, full daylight, water dark blue and legible edge to edge, no glare. Wave is weak wind-textured windswell over the reef: short crumbly lines that stand up briefly and reform, plenty of surface chop from the 18g22kt N cross-shore. Not closeouts in the classic sense, just gutless - no green wall with a shoulder running off the lip in any of the 3 detail frames or 6 sheet frames. Scanned the takeoff zone, both shoulders and the inside channel in every detail frame and both crowd frames: no bodies anywhere in the water, no boards, no paddling lines. Confident 0 out. Cam framed on the water, land count not applicable

08:56 sunrise run. Morning sun is low from the right and lights the cliff and buildings warm, but the water itself is fully readable this run - no blowout, unlike the 18:05 run. The bay is effectively flat: uniform wind ripple with a couple of soft knee-high reforms crossing the inside near the rocks and a wash on the point. No swell line stands up anywhere in the 3 detail frames. Scanned the whole open bay, the corner by the rocks and the shorebreak in every detail and crowd frame: nobody in the water at all. 0 out, and given how flat it is that is unsurprising rather than a missed-opportunity empty lineup. Cam framed on the water, land count not applicable

08:56 sunrise run. No images this run - the HLS stream at hls.cdn-surfline.com/ireland/pt-ribeiradeilhas/playlist.m3u8 returned 404 Not Found and ffmpeg failed, so collect.py wrote no sheet, crowd or detail crop. No vision read is possible: surfers and people both null. This is a dead cam, NOT an empty lineup - and it matters, because Ribeira is the one spot rated FAIR this run with the N wind blowing offshore there, so it is the spot most likely to have people on it. Metrics still collected normally

08:56 sunrise run, wide distant cam so all counts approximate. Cam is clean and bright with no glare this morning. Wave is small and wind-chopped: a broad band of whitewater rolling in across the sand with a slightly better peak on the bank near the headland, nothing with a proper wall. In the water there is a loose cluster of dark specks sitting outside the whitewater in the right-hand third of the frame - roughly 5 at the higher of the two crowd frames, plus one or two closer in near the rocks in the detail frames. At this range a surfer and a bodyboarder are indistinguishable, so ~5 out is approximate. On land: a group of about 5 in pink jerseys standing together on the sand by the rocks (looks like a surf-school or lifeguard group) plus 4-5 scattered sitting figures along the waterline, so roughly 10 on the sand - approximate. Beach is near-empty for the hour

18:05 sunset run. Low sun from the left but the Norte frame stays legible - water is dark blue, no blowout. Wave is a weak wind-textured shorebreak: small crumbly reforming lines close in, nothing standing up outside, no green wall in any of the 3 detail frames. Scanned takeoff zone, shoulder and inside channel in every detail and crowd frame: one dark body in the water mid-frame at +0s on the crowd crop, and a second reddish figure with what looks like a board in the shorebreak at +37s; the +25s detail frame shows an orange/red figure prone in the wash. Calling 2 in the water, and they read as bodyboarders/swimmers in the shorebreak rather than surfers on a wave. Two or three people on the promenade at the bottom edge of the sheet frames but the cam is framed on the water, so land count not applicable

18:05 sunset run. Low sun sits directly in the left third of the Sul frame and blows it to pure white - that is exactly where the beach and takeoff zone are. The readable right-hand half of the bay (open water, the point and the outer rock) is empty across all 3 detail frames and both crowd frames, but the part of the water that matters is unreadable, so recording surfers as null rather than claiming an empty lineup. Wave read from the legible half: effectively flat - uniform wind ripple, the only whitewater is a wash on the rocks under the point and a boil over the outer rock, no swell line standing up. Cam framed on the water, land count not applicable

18:05 sunset run. Cam is back up after last run's 404, but the detail and crowd crops are aimed too high this run - both are filled with open horizon and a lamp post, with the lineup off the bottom of the frame, so the magnified crops are useless for counting. On the wide contact sheet the surf zone sits under the sun glare track and I cannot resolve boards from bathers there, so surfers = null rather than a guess. There is one small dark object bottom-left of the +0s crowd frame that could be a surfer but I will not count it. Wave read from the sheet: small clean waist-high lines coming in with the strong N offshore holding them up - the best-looking water of the four spots. Land is countable and busy: people spread the full width of the sand, a line of them along the waterline and more on the promenade rail - roughly 50, approximate

18:05 sunset run, wide distant cam so all counts approximate. The camera looks straight into the setting sun and the entire surf zone is blown to white in all 3 detail frames and both crowd frames - the break line is not readable at all. Several figures stand at the waterline in the wash but nobody is resolvable seaward of the whitewater, and at this range a bodyboarder and a bather look identical, so surfers = null. Not an empty lineup - a glared-out cam. Wave read is limited to the darker left corner by the headland, where the wash on the rocks and a broad band of whitewater along the sand suggests the usual weak wind-blown shorebreak. Land is the readable half: still a busy end-of-August beach with umbrellas, sunbathers and walkers across the sand - roughly 60, approximate
